claims.text: The dynamic behavior of as-solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn is primarily governed by a temperature- and strain-rate-mediated transition in dislocation slip mechanisms.
Low temperature and high strain rate restrict dislocation cross-slip and dynamic recovery in FeNiCrMn.
Restricted cross-slip and dynamic recovery promote dislocation accumulation and pile-up.
Low-temperature, high-strain-rate deformation may produce limited deformation twins.
Dislocation pile-up and restricted mobility at low temperature and high strain rate increase yield strength.
Dislocation pile-up and restricted mobility at low temperature and high strain rate reduce ductility.
Higher temperature and lower strain rate enhance dislocation cross-slip and dynamic recovery.
Enhanced cross-slip and dynamic recovery at high temperature and low strain rate lower flow stress and yield strength.
Enhanced cross-slip and dynamic recovery at high temperature and low strain rate sustain ductility.
Stacking-fault-energy effects govern the evolving dislocation configurations and possible twin boundaries.
Significant grain refinement, secondary phases, or introduced extrinsic defects may change the proposed mechanism.
The relevant initial material retains a typical casting-derived grain structure and inherent dislocation density after homogenization.
